title: Real sprites, a boss fight, and a bug I didn't write
content:
## Real sprites, a boss fight, and a bug I didn't write

Spent the last couple days on Sanctuary of Spirits and it finally stopped looking like a tech demo held together with emoji.

**The sprites are real now.** Every entity — player, the three enemy types, wild spirits, the boss — was just a Unicode emoji in a div up until now. Cute for prototyping, useless for anything I'd actually want someone to look at. So I hand-authored 32×32 pixel grids (character-per-pixel, mapped through a palette table) and wrote a small generator script that renders them to PNG instead of exporting art from some editor. Means the art is just text in the repo — I can diff it, tweak a single pixel in code, regenerate. Player's a gnome warlock now, the stalkers are shadow hounds, there's a cursed-mask lurker and a wendigo stag dasher. No blur anywhere — `image-rendering: pixelated`, everything scaled by integer factors only.

**Added an actual boss.** There's a Disturbed Grave seeded 26-34 tiles out from the Sanctuary on a random bearing every run. Interact with it and a Corrupted Vanguard Knight wakes up — heavier, tankier, moves every other tick instead of every tick like the regular enemies, hits for 2 instead of 1. Kill him and it's a guaranteed relic plus a chunk of ectoplasm. Also finally capped the world — the forest used to generate forever, which sounds cool until you realize infinite exploration with no stakes is just walking. Now there's a hard zone radius; past it the world turns to dead impassable forest, so the grave is always findable and always finite.

**Extraction is in.** Loot from a run doesn't count until you walk it back inside a radius of home — die out there before that and you drop half of whatever's unbanked. That plus the boss gives the run shape something to actually push against, instead of just "walk around clicking on bushes."

**Worker economy has teeth now.** You can assign rescued spirits to gather wood or ectoplasm passively while you're out in the woods. Sounds free. It isn't — a spirit on task corrupts 1.5x faster than one just idling at the Sanctuary. So every spirit you put to work is a countdown you started on purpose. That tension is basically the whole management loop and it wasn't really *felt* until the rate numbers landed right.

**Also added a real cold open.** Four-scene cutscene before you drop into the woods — decree, fracture, exile, sanctuary — typewriter text, crossfades, skippable. Gives the corruption mechanic and the whole "why am I doing this" some actual weight instead of just spawning you in a forest with a lantern and no context.

**Least fun part of the week:** wild spirits stopped spawning correctly and I lost an embarrassing amount of time to it before finding that a destructuring line had quietly dropped `wildSpirits` entirely during an earlier AI-assisted pass — the array was just never being read from state. Left myself a comment in the source so future-me remembers to actually diff what these tools touch instead of trusting the diff summary. Fixed now, rescues work again.

**Still rough:** only one difficulty tier is actually wired up even though the code's been talking about Gentle/Normal/Cursed for a while, macOS build isn't notarized yet so Gatekeeper will complain on a fresh machine, and combat balance around the Vanguard fight needs another pass — right now beating him is more about kiting than any real skill expression.

Next up is probably notarization and getting the difficulty picker actually functional before I touch anything else cosmetic.
